title: Runtime semver exception policy and LTS branching guidelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define an operationally-safe semantic versioning policy for the Redwood serving runtime that balances developer ergonomics with production stability. This ticket codifies rules for what constitutes a major/minor/patch change, the conditions under which a 'semver exception' is allowed, LTS branch behavior, deprecation windows, required automated checks, and the upgrade tooling and guardrails that must exist before making breaking changes.

Scope: runtime APIs (HTTP/gRPC surface used by Redwood API), on-disk model/layout formats (KV cache/serialization), public CLI/SDK behaviors that customers may script against, and RPC/ABI between orchestration and serving nodes. Not in scope: internal-only metrics, ephemeral debug endpoints, or internal operator CLIs that are not supported for customer automation.

Key definitions (operational):
- Breaking change (Major): Any change that can cause existing customer requests or pinned deployments to fail or change semantics without opt-in. Examples: removal of an RPC field, incompatible model serialization format change, change to the runtime's request routing semantics that can silently alter tokenization or outputs.
- Backwards-compatible behavioral change (Minor): New features or non-breaking API additions, performance improvements that preserve API/ABI.
- Patch: Bugfixes, performance patches, non-functional changes that do not alter API/ABI.
- Semver exception: A narrowly-scoped, pre-approved deviation from strict semver semantics when the operational cost of maintaining two variants exceeds the customer risk, provided compensating controls exist (canary gating, automatic rollbacks, retry-safe fallback model).
acceptance_criteria: A concise semver policy doc (this ticket) reviewed and approved by Release Engineering, Runtime, PM, and Security
A gating checklist (CI jobs + runtime invariant checks) added to runtime PR template that validates compatibility markers
A migration plan template for any major change that includes: deprecation announcement timeline (>=8 weeks), migration helper scripts or shims, and automated rollback plan
An LTS branching diagram and policy: how bugfixes and security patches are backported, how long an LTS receives patches (>=12 months), and when to cut a new LTS
A prototype CLI 'upgrade-assistant' that can detect runtime version skew across clusters and surface incompatible nodes
Documentation and a public-facing changelog format for breaking changes with migration steps

implementation_notes:
Planned engineering work:
- Add runtime ABI tag to all model packages and embed runtime_version + abi_version in the model manifest.
- Require buf-based protobuf compatibility checks in CI for any proto changes.
- Implement optional compatibility shim layer that can deserialize both old and new model formats for at least 1 major version window where feasible.
- Add 'compat-check' job in release pipeline: spins up a canary cluster with mixed runtime versions and runs the canonical test-suite (deterministic prompts + golden outputs).
- Upgrade-assistant: CLI that queries Console API to report version skew and suggests per-customer remediation steps.
- Changelog format: structured JSON changelogs published with each release, with machine-readable 'breaking' flags for automated tooling.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Customers pin runtime versions and rely on fragile on-disk formats. Mitigation: enforce deprecation windows, require shims or migration tools before allowing removal of a format, and use rollout gates and telemetry to detect regressions.
Risk: Large refactor may be classified as an 'exception' and slip through. Mitigation: semver-exception review board (Release Eng + Runtime + Security + PM) that signs off on exceptions and records compensating controls.
Risk: Automation gaps allow incompatible releases into hosted regions. Mitigation: block publishing to production channels until 'compat-check' CI succeeds and human reviewer verifies migration artifacts.
operational_playbook:
Before cutting a major (breaking) release:
1) Create a migration RFC and link migration scripts
2) Add deprecation banners in Console with dates and migration docs
3) Run compat-check with mixed-version canaries for 72h and verify no request failures above baseline
4) Run customer-impact simulation (sample 1% of active deployments) and evaluate errors
5) Stage rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on error thresholds
6) Post-rollout: 7-day regression monitoring and incident review if anomalies detected
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on: the definition of 'semver exception' and the approval process, the length of deprecation windows (currently 8 weeks), and the scope of the prototype upgrade-assistant CLI. Security must confirm the threat-model step for any change touching model key material or KMS interactions. Ready for Release Eng + Runtime + PM + Security review.
